newsitem.title: CHINA: HK's Tung says too early to speculate on tax cuts.
newsitem.headline: HK's Tung says too early to speculate on tax cuts.

text.p: Hong Kong's chief executive Tung Chee-hwa said on Thursday that it was too early to speculate on whether corporate profit taxes could be cut.
"It's too early to speculate on this issue," Tung told a gathering at the Australian Chamber of Commerce.
Tung said the government was considering "many fundamental issues" and that answers to these questions would be delivered in due course.
"I think it is important to recognize that we will continue a very prudent fiscal policy, which is one of the reasons for our success," he said.
The chief executive said the government would continue to ponder the best way to use Hong Kong's large fiscal surplus.

"Some of it (could be used) in special areas of services or in providing greater incentives in reducing taxes. Or it may be used in investment in making Hong Kong more competitive in areas of infrastructure," Tung said.
Turning to the issue of housing, Tung reiterated his view that the best way to deal with Hong Kong's problem of inadequate housing supply and rising prices was to increase supply.
"The only way to tackle rising prices is to provide adequate long-term supply of housing," he said.
Tung said the government was determined to meet its goal of providing 85,000 new flats per year over the next decade.
He said that at the end of 10 years, the government would like to see 70 percent of Hong Kong people living in homes they own, compared with about 51 percent now.
"I have every confidence and every reason to believe this is possible because fundamentally there is land in Hong Kong and secondly we have the financial resources in Hong Kong," he said.
"I believe we have the priority as well as the determination to make it work," Tung said.
